content: Engaging in Bodhisattva Conduct0. IntroductionIn the language of India: BodhicaryāvatāraIn the Tibetan language: Engaging in Bodhisattva ConductHomage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!1. Chapter One: Explaining the Benefits of the Mind of AwakeningI bow respectfully to the buddhas, their spiritual children,who embody the truth, and all worthy ones.I will briefly explain, in accordance with the scriptures,how to engage in the vows of the spiritual children of the buddhas.I will not state anything here that has not been said before.Nor do I possess skill in composition.Therefore, I have no intention of benefiting others.I composed this for the sake of cultivating my own mind.Through these words, the strength of my faithwill temporarily increase for the sake of cultivating good deeds.And if others, who share my fortune,see these words, may they be meaningful.This opportunity is very hard to find.Having attained the ability to accomplish human purpose,if one does not accomplish what is beneficial in this life,how will this opportunity arise again later?Just as a flash of lightning briefly illuminatesa dark, cloudy night,likewise, rarely, through the power of the buddhas,does a virtuous state of mind arise.Therefore, consider that good deeds are weak,while misdeeds are powerful and unbearable.What other virtue, besides the perfect Mind of Awakening,could overcome them?The mighty Sages, who reflected deeply for many eons,reflected that this alone is beneficial.By this, countless beingseasily attain supreme happiness.Wishing to overcome hundreds of cyclic existence’s sufferings,wishing to remove beings’ unhappiness,and wishing to experience hundreds of joys,one should always hold fast to the Mind of Awakening.When the Mind of Awakening arises, in a single moment,those wretched ones bound in the prison of cyclic existenceare called spiritual children of the buddhas,and become worthy of homage by gods and humans alike.Like the supreme elixir that transforms base metals into gold,having taken this impure body, it transforms it into the immeasurable,precious body of a buddha.Therefore, hold fast to what is called the Mind of Awakening.The sole guide of beings, with immeasurable wisdom,upon proper examination, finds it precious.Therefore, those who wish to be free from the states of sufferingshould firmly hold fast to the precious Mind of Awakening.All other good deeds, like a plantain plant,produce fruit and then perish.But the tree of the Mind of Awakening alwaysproduces fruit and grows inexhaustibly.Even if one has committed extremely unbearable misdeeds,relying on a hero, like relying on one who dispels great fear,why would the wise not rely on thatwhich quickly liberates one?Therefore, it certainly burns away great misdeedsin a single moment, like the fire at the end of an eon.Its immeasurable benefitswere explained by Maitreya, the wise and excellent one.To summarize, the Mind of Awakeningshould be understood in two aspects:the aspiring mind of awakeningand the engaging mind of awakening.Just as one knows the differencebetween wishing to go and actually going,likewise, the wise should understandthe difference between these two in order.From the aspiring mind of awakening,great fruit arises in cyclic existence,but it does not continuously produce meritin the same way as the engaging mind.From the moment one correctly takesthat resolve,the irreversible resolve,to liberate all countless beings,from that moment on, even when asleepor careless, the strength of meritcontinuously arises in abundance,equal to space.This was taught by the buddhas themselvesfor the benefit of humble beings,in response to a reasonable requestfrom the bodhisattva Bhadrapāla.If one merely thinks,"May I relieve the headache of a single being,"that person, endowed with the intention to help,possesses immeasurable merit.So what need is there to speakof one who wishes to remove the immeasurable unhappinessof every single being,and to accomplish immeasurable good qualities for each?Whether it be a father or a mother,who possesses such a benevolent mind?Whether it be gods or sages,does even Brahma possess this?If, in the past,for one's own sake,one has not even dreamed of such a thought,how could it arise for the sake of others?That intention for the benefit of beings,which does not arise even for one's own sake in others,this precious and exceptional mind,is an unprecedented wonder that has arisen.What measure can there befor the merit of this precious mind,which is the cause of joy for all beings,and the elixir for the suffering of beings?If merely intending to benefitis superior to worshipping the buddhas,what need is there to speak of the effortto bring about the happiness of all beings without exception?Though beings wish to abandon suffering,they rush directly into suffering itself.Though they wish for happiness, through ignorance,they destroy their own happiness like an enemy.Whoever wishes to satisfy with all happinessthose who are deprived of happinessand filled with much suffering,and to cut off all suffering,and also removes delusion—where is there a virtue equal to that?Where is there such a friend?Where is there such merit?If even one who repays kindnessis temporarily worthy of praise,what need is there to speak of a bodhisattvawho acts kindly without being asked?People honor as virtuous one who offersa small amount of ordinary food to beings,giving it only briefly each time, though regularly,or satisfying them for half a day with disdain.What need is there to speak of the continuous generositythat fulfills all the wishesof countless beings for a long time,leading to the unsurpassed happiness of the buddhas?The Sage taught that if anyonegenerates an evil thought towards such a spiritual child,that person will remain in hell for as many eonsas the number of evil thoughts generated.However, if one generates a pure mind,its fruit will increase even more.Even with great effort, no misdeeds arisefor the spiritual children, and good deeds naturally increase.I bow to the body of one in whomthat precious and supreme mind has arisen.I take refuge in that source of happiness,who, even when harmed, brings about happiness.This concludes the first chapter of Engaging in Bodhisattva Conduct, "Explaining the Benefits of the Mind of Awakening."2. Chapter Two: Confession of MisdeedsTo take hold of the precious Mind of Awakening,I offer excellent homage to the buddhas, the sacred Dharma,the pure jewels, and the spiritual children,who are oceans of good qualities.Whatever flowers and fruits exist,whatever kinds of medicine exist,whatever worldly jewels exist,and whatever pure, delightful water exists,precious mountains, and likewise,forests and places that are secluded and delightful,trees adorned with blossoms,and trees whose branches bend with fine fruits,and in the realms of gods and others, fragrances,incense, wish-granting trees, and jewel trees,various kinds of uncultivated crops,and other ornaments worthy of offering,lakes and ponds adorned with lotuses,with swans uttering very sweet and delightful sounds,all those unowned things,reaching to the ends of the boundless expanse of space,I take them in my mind and offer them well to the Supreme Sage,together with his spiritual children.May the supreme recipients, the Great Compassionate Ones,consider me with kindness and accept these offerings of mine.I am devoid of merit and greatly poor;I have no other wealth for offerings.Therefore, may the Protectors, who intend the benefit of others,accept these for my sake, by their own power.To the buddhas and their spiritual children, Ipermanently offer my entire body.May the Supreme Beings completely accept me.With reverence, I will become your servant.Since I am completely accepted by you,I will be fearless in cyclic existence and benefit beings.I will truly turn away from former misdeeds,and I will never commit other misdeeds again.In a very fragrant bathing chamber,with a crystal floor, clear and gleaming, spread out,with delightful pillars blazing with jewels,and canopies shimmering with pearls,I offer ritual bathing to the buddhas and their spiritual children,with many jewel vases filled with delightful, pure water,accompanied by various songsand musical instruments.Then, I dry their bodies with unparalleled garments,pure and imbued with sweet fragrance.After that, I offer them excellent, dyed,very fragrant, supreme robes.With various fine, delicate, and soft garments,and hundreds of supreme ornaments,I adorn Noble Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī,Avalokiteśvara, and others.With supreme fragrances, whose sweet scentfills the triple world, I anoint the bodies of all the mighty Sages,who are radiant and blazing,like refined, polished gold.To the mighty Sages, the supreme recipients of offerings,I offer delightful Mandarava flowers, lotuses,utpalas, and all other fragrant flowers,and well-arranged, delightful garlands.I also offer to them clouds of incense,with supreme, captivating, pervasive fragrance.I also offer to them various divine foods,consisting of edibles and drinks.I also offer jewel lamps,with golden lotuses arranged in rows.On the ground, spread and anointed with incense,I scatter delightful loose flowers.I also offer immeasurable palaces, filled with delightful praises,adorned with beautiful, blazing pearl and jewel hangings,which are boundless ornaments of space,to those whose nature is compassion.Beautiful jewel parasols with golden handles,whose fringes are adorned with delightful ornaments,well-shaped and lovely to behold, hoisted aloft,I always offer to all the mighty Sages.Furthermore, may clouds of offerings,with delightful, sweet musical sounds,arise everywhere, individually,satisfying the sufferings of beings.May showers of jewels, flowers, and so forth,continuously fallupon all the sacred Dharma jewels,stupas, and statues.Just as Mañjuśrī and othersmade offerings to the buddhas,likewise, I offer homage to the buddhas,the Protectors, and their spiritual children.To the oceans of good qualities, Ioffer praise with oceans of verses of praise.May clouds of sweet praisesdefinitely arise everywhere.To all the buddhas who passed in the three times,together with the Dharma and the supreme assembly,I bow with bodiesas numerous as all the atoms of the universe.I bow to the foundations of the Mind of Awakening,and to the stupas.Likewise, I bow to the masters, teachers,and the supreme practitioners.Until I attain awakening,I go for refuge to the buddhas.Likewise, I go for refuge to the Dharmaand the assembly of bodhisattvas.To the fully enlightened Buddhas and bodhisattvas,who reside in all directions,and who embody great compassion,I join my palms and pray:From beginningless cyclic existence,in this life or in others,whatever misdeeds I unknowingly committed,or caused to be committed,overwhelmed by delusion and confusion,and whatever I rejoiced in,having seen those faults,I confess them to the Protectors from the heart.Whatever harm I committed with body, speech,and mind, driven by troubling emotions,towards the Three Jewels,my parents, or other suffering beings,whatever extremely unbearable wrongdoingsI, a wrongdoer tainted by many faults,have committed,I confess all of them to the guides.I will die beforemy misdeeds are purified.Please protect me swiftly,so that I may definitely be freed from this.This unreliable Lord of Deathdoes not wait for what is done or undone.Therefore, everyone, whether sick or not,cannot rely on fleeting life.I did not understand that I mustabandon everything and depart.For the sake of friends and enemies,I committed various misdeeds.My enemies will cease to exist,and my friends will also cease to exist.I too will cease to exist,and likewise, everything will cease to exist.Just like experiences in a dream,whatever things were enjoyed,those will become objects of memory.All that has passed will not be seen.For the time being, in this very life,many friends and enemies have passed away.The unbearable misdeeds committed for their sakeremain before me.I did not realizethat I am fleeting.Therefore, through delusion, attachment, and hatred,I committed many kinds of misdeeds.This life continuously diminishes,never staying for a day or night.If there is no increase from elsewhere,why would I not die?While I sit on my bed,surrounded by all my relatives and friends,I will experience the sensations of departing lifeall by myself.When seized by the Lord of Death's messengers,what good are relatives, what good are friends?If merit alone can protect me at that time,I did not rely on it.Protectors, I, being careless,did not realize this great fear.For the sake of this impermanent life,I accumulated many misdeeds.Even someone led to a place of execution todaybecomes terrified.If their face appears dry, with bad eyes, and so forth,and seems different from before,what need is there to speak of oneseized by terrifying messengers of the Lord of Death,afflicted by a great illness,and utterly wretched?"Who will protect me well from this great fear?"With wide, terrified eyes,they search for refugein all four directions.Having seen that there is no refuge in any direction,they then become utterly despondent.If there is no refuge in that situation,what will I do then?Therefore, to the buddhas, the Protectors of beings,who strive for the sake of protecting beings,and who are powerful and dispel all fears,I go for refuge from this very day.Likewise, I truly go for refuge to the Dharma,which is realized by themand dispels the fears of cyclic existence,and to the assembly of bodhisattvas.I, terrified by fear,offer myself to Samantabhadra.I offer my bodyto Mañjuśrī.To Protector Avalokiteśvara,whose compassionate conduct is unfailing,I cry out with a wretched voice.Please protect me, a wrongdoer!To Noble Ākāśagarbha,Kṣitigarbha,and all the greatly compassionate Protectors,I cry out from my heart, seeking refuge.I go for refuge to Vajrapāṇi,who, upon seeing them, causes the messengers of the Lord of Deathand other enemies to flee in terrorin all four directions.In the past, I transgressed your words.Now, having seen great fear,I go for refuge to you.Please quickly dispel my fear.If one must act according to a doctor's wordseven when afraid of an ordinary illness,what need is there to speak of oneconstantly afflicted by the illness of hundreds of faults, such as attachment?That single fault can destroyall people dwelling on earth.If no other medicine to cure themcan be found anywhere,then to disregard the words of the all-knowing doctor,who extracts all piercing pains,is an act of extreme delusionand a cause for scorn.If one must be carefuleven on a small, ordinary precipice,what need is there to speak ofa long precipice, falling for thousands of miles?It is not right to sit happily,thinking, "I will not die today."The time when I will cease to existwill certainly come.Who will grant me fearlessness?How will I definitely be freed from this?If I will certainly cease to exist,how can my mind be at ease?What remains of mefrom what I experienced and perished in the past?I clung to that,and transgressed the words of my guru.If I must abandon this life,and likewise, my relatives and friends,and go somewhere alone,what good are all my friends and enemies?Suffering arises from unwholesome deeds."How will I definitely be freed from that?"It is right for me to thinkonly of this, day and night.Whatever misdeeds I committed,whether inherently harmful or prohibited,due to my ignorance and delusion,I confess all of them.Before the Protectors, directly,with palms joined, and with fear of suffering,I repeatedly prostrate,and confess all those misdeeds.May the guides consider my misdeedsas faults.Since this is not good,I will never commit them again.This concludes the second chapter of Engaging in Bodhisattva Conduct, "Confession of Misdeeds."3. Chapter Three: Taking Hold of the Mind of AwakeningI rejoice in the good deedsthat bring rest from the suffering of all beingsin the lower realms,and in the happiness of those who suffer.I rejoice in the good deeds accumulatedthat are the cause of awakening.I rejoice in the definite liberationof embodied beings from the suffering of cyclic existence.I also rejoice in the awakening of the protectorsand the bodhisattvas on the paths.I rejoice with joyin the ocean of good deeds—the Mind of Awakening—that brings happiness to all beings,and in the acts that benefit beings.I bow with palms joined to the buddhas in all directionsand pray:“Please light the lamp of the teachingsfor beings bewildered by the darkness of suffering.”I bow with palms joined to the buddhas who wish to pass beyond sorrowand pray:“Please do not abandon these blind beings,but remain for countless eons.”Having done all these things,whatever good deeds I have accumulated,may all the suffering of all beingsbe removed by them.For as long as there are sick beings,until their illnesses are cured,may I be medicine, a doctor,and their nurse.May I rain down food and drink,removing the suffering of hunger and thirst.During the eons of famine,may I become food and drink.For beings who are destitute and poor,may I become an inexhaustible treasure.May all kinds of necessitiesappear before them.My body, as well as my possessions,and all my good deeds of the three times,I give away without reservationto accomplish the benefit of all beings.By giving up everything, one passes beyond sorrow.My mind accomplishes passing beyond sorrow.Giving up everything is the same for all,but giving to beings is supreme.I have given this body to all embodied beings,to do with it as they please.Therefore, they are free to always kill, insult,beat, or do whatever else they wish.Even if they make sport of my body,or make it the object of their mockery and derision,I have already given this body away,so what is the use of fussing over it?Let them do whatever actionswill not harm them.May no one ever act pointlesslyby focusing on me.If anyone becomes angry or faithfulby focusing on me,may that itself alwaysbe the cause for accomplishing all their aims.Whoever speaks ill of me,or harms others,or slanders them,may all of them attain awakening.May I be a protector for the unprotected,a guide for those on the path,a boat,a raft, and a bridge for those who wish to cross.May I be an island for those desiring an island,a resting place for those desiring a resting place.May I become a servant for allbeings who wish for a servant.May I become a wish-fulfilling jewel, an excellent vase,an accomplished spell, a great medicine,a wish-granting tree,and a wish-granting cow for embodied beings.Like the great elements of earth and so forth,and like space, may I alwaysbe the basis of various kinds of sustenancefor countless beings.Likewise, for all beingsreaching to the ends of space,until all pass beyond sorrow,may I be the cause of their sustenance.Just as the buddhas of the pastgenerated the Mind of Awakening,and remained in the bodhisattva trainingin that sequence,likewise, for the benefit of beings,I will generate the Mind of Awakening.And likewise, I will trainin the training in that sequence.In this way, the wise one,having taken up the excellent Mind of Awakening,strengthens the mind as followsto also cause it to flourish:Today my life is fruitful.I have perfectly obtained human existence.Today I am born into the family of the buddhas.Today I have become a spiritual child of the buddhas.Now, by whatever means, I willundertake actions befitting my family.I will act so that this pure, noble familyis not defiled.Just as a blind personmight find a jewel in a heap of rubbish,likewise, by some chance,this Mind of Awakening has arisen in me.This is the supreme nectarthat conquers the Lord of Death for beings.This is also the inexhaustible treasurethat removes the poverty of beings.This is also the supreme medicinethat perfectly cures the illnesses of beings.It is a resting tree for beingswho wander and are weary on the road of existence.It is a bridge that deliversall beings from the lower realms.It is the moon that has risento clear away the torment of the disturbing emotions of beings.It is the great sun that entirely removesthe confusion and blurred vision of beings.It is the essence of butter that emergedfrom churning the milk of the sacred teachings.For the great guests—beings traveling on the road of existencewho wish to enjoy the delights of happiness—this is the supreme source of happiness,and it satisfies them.Today, before all the protectors, I haveinvited all beings to buddhahoodand to happiness in the interim.Therefore, gods, demigods, and others, rejoice!This concludes the third chapter of Engaging in Bodhisattva Conduct, "Taking Hold of the Mind of Awakening."4. Chapter Four: Teaching on CarefulnessHaving firmly taken hold of the Mind of Awakening,the spiritual children of the buddhasshould always strive without strayingfrom the training.Whatever has been undertaken rashly,or whatever has not been properly examined,even if a vow has been made,it is right to examine whether to do it or abandon it.What the buddhas and their spiritual childrenhave examined with great wisdom,and what I myself have examined and re-examined—what reason is there to turn away from that?If, having made such a vow,I do not accomplish the task,having deceived all those beings,what will my destiny be like?It is said that if a personmerely thinks of giving even a small, ordinary thing,but does not give it,that person will become a hungry ghost.If, having sincerely invitedall beings to unsurpassed happiness,I then deceive them all,how can I go to happy realms?Even if a person abandons the Mind of Awakening,the way they are set freeis inconceivable karma,known only by the all-knowing.For a bodhisattva, thisis the heaviest of downfalls.If this occurs,it diminishes the benefit for all beings.If anyone obstructs this meriteven for a moment,having diminished the benefit for beings,their lower realms will be endless.If the happiness of a single beingis destroyed, I myself will be harmed.Needless to say, if the happiness of countlessbeings, filling all of space, is destroyed!Thus, if powerful downfallsand the powerful Mind of Awakeningalternate in cyclic existence,it will take a long time to attain the stages.Therefore, just as I have vowed,I will respectfully accomplish it.If I do not strive from now on,I will go lower and lower.Countless buddhas, who benefit all beings,have passed.But I, due to my own faults,was not within the sphere of their healing.If I continue to act in the same way,it will be the same again and again.In the lower realms, I will experienceillness, bondage, cutting, piercing, and so forth.When will I obtainsuch a rare human body,the appearance of a buddha,faith, and the ability to practice virtue?This life, free from illness,with food and without harm,is fleeting and deceptive;the body is like a temporary loan.With such conduct,I will not obtain a human body.If I do not obtain a human body,there will be only misdeeds and no good deeds.If, when I have the fortune to practice virtue,I do not perform good deeds,and am bewildered by all the suffering of the lower realms,what will I be able to do then?If I have not performed good deeds,and have accumulated misdeeds,even for a hundred million eons,I will not even hear the word "happy realms."Therefore, the Blessed One taughtthat a human body is extremely hard to obtain,like a turtle putting its neckthrough the hole of a yoke in a vast ocean.If even a single moment of misdeedcan cause one to dwell in the lowest hell for an eon,needless to say, if misdeeds accumulated in beginningless cyclic existencewill prevent one from going to happy realms!Even after experiencing that much,one is not set free.For while experiencing it,other misdeeds arise.If, having found such an opportunity,I do not cultivate virtue,there is no greater deception than this,and no greater foolishness than this.If, having understood this,I later become lazy due to delusion,at the time of death,great sorrow will arise.If the unbearable fires of hellburn my body for a long time,my mind will surely be tormentedby the blazing fire of unbearable regret.If, having somehow foundthis extremely rare and beneficial ground,I, being endowed with knowledge,am again led to hell,it is as if I have been deluded by a spell.I simply have no mind here.I do not know what deludes me;what is within me?Enemies such as hatred and cravingdo not possess hands or feet.Yet, in some way, though not brave or wise,they have made me their slave.While dwelling in my mind,they harm me with delight.Not to be angry at them, but to endure—this is inappropriate patience, a cause for scorn.Even if all gods and demigodsrise up as my enemies,they cannot lead meinto the fire of the lowest hell.But this powerful enemy, defilement,when it encounters anyone, even Mount Meruwill be reduced to ashes, leaving nothing.It casts me into that in a single instant.My enemy, defilement,has been an enemy continuously for a beginningless time.No other enemycan last for such a long time.If I serve my friends respectfully,they all bring benefit and happiness.But if I rely on defilements,they again inflict suffering and harm.How can I be fearless and joyful in cyclic existenceif this enemy, which has been a continuous foe for so long,the sole cause for the increase of all harm,is truly established in my heart?How can I have happinessif these enemies, who are the guardians of the prison of cyclic existence,and have become executioners in hell and so forth,dwell in the net of attachment in my mind?As long as I have not truly conquered this enemy,I will not abandon my striving here.If those puffed up with pridebecome angry even at a minor hindrance, they cannot sleep until it is conquered.If, when defilements, which are naturally mortal and cause suffering,are arrayed on the battlefield, one wishes to conquer them forcefully,and disregards the suffering of being struck by arrows, spears, and weapons,and does not retreat without accomplishing the purpose,then, for me, who strives to conquerthis enemy, which is the cause of all suffering,and is naturally an enemy,needless to say, I will not become disheartened or despondent by any of the hundreds of causes of suffering!If a meaningless enemy inflicts wounds,and one cherishes them as if they were ornaments on the body,then for me, who strives to accomplish a great purpose,why should suffering be a harm?If fishermen, hunters, farmers, and so forth,who only think of their own livelihood,endure the harm of cold, heat, and so forth,why should I not endure it for the happiness of beings?When I vowed to liberateall beings, filling the ten directions of space,from defilements,I myself was not yet free from defilements.How is it not madnessto speak without knowing my own measure?Therefore, I must alwaysbe unwavering in conquering defilements.I must cling to this,hold a grudge, and wage battle.Such defilementsare nothing but the destroyers of defilements.Even if I am burned and killed,or my head is cut off,I will never surrenderto the enemy of defilements.An ordinary enemy, even if driven from one land,will dwell in another land,gather strength, and return from there.The enemy of defilement is not like that.Defilements are abandoned by the eye of wisdom.Once removed from my mind, where will they go?Where will they dwell and return to harm me?Clinging to the mind is merely striving for myself.Defilements do not dwell in objects, nor in the sense faculties, nor in between.Nor are they elsewhere. So where do these things dwell that harm all beings?This is like an illusion. Therefore, abandon fear in your heart and strive to know.Why do they needlessly inflict harm on me in hell and so forth?Having reflected in this way,I must strive to accomplish the training as explained.If a patient does not listen to the doctor's words,how can that patient, needing treatment, be cured by medicines?This concludes the fourth chapter of Engaging in Bodhisattva Conduct, "Teaching on Carefulness."5. Chapter Five: Guarding AwarenessThose who wish to uphold the trainingmust guard their minds with great effort.If this mind is not guarded,the training cannot be upheld.Just as an untamed, wild elephantinflicts immeasurable harm,a wild, untamed mind-elephantdoes not inflict such harm in this world.If the mind-elephant is firmly boundwith the rope of mindfulness,all fears will cease,and all good deeds will come to hand.Tigers, lions, elephants, bears,snakes, and all enemies,the guardians of the hell realms,and likewise sorcerers and demons—By binding this single mind,all those are bound.By taming this single mind,all those are tamed.The Buddha taught that all these fearsand immeasurable sufferingarise from the mind.This is truly what he taught.Who intentionally createdthe weapons of the hell beings?Who made the burning iron ground?From what did those heaps of fire arise?The Sage taught that all such thingsare the result of harmful thoughts.Thus, in the three realms,there is no other fear than the mind.If giving to the pooris the perfection of generosity,and if there are still poor beings, then howdid the protectors perfect generosity before?The perfection of generosity is taughtas the mind of relinquishment,giving away all possessions with fruitful intentto all beings. Therefore, it is the mind itself.Wherever fish and other creaturesare driven away so they are not killed,when the intention to desist is attained,it is taught as the perfection of discipline.Unruly beings are like space;they cannot be overcome.If this single angry mind is conquered,it is like conquering all those enemies.How could there be enough leatherto cover all the surface of the earth?It is like covering the entire earthwith just a piece of leather for a shoe sole.Likewise, I cannot turn awayexternal things.I should turn away this mind of mine;what need is there to turn away others?What fruit arises from generating a single clear mind,like that of Brahmā and other gods?The fruit of actions of body and speechis not like that due to weaker conduct.Even if one performs all recitationsand ascetic practices for a long time,the wise teach that what is done with a distracted mindis meaningless.Whoever does not know this secret of the mind,the supreme essence of the teachings,even if they wish to attain happiness and conquer suffering,they wander aimlessly without purpose.Therefore, this mind of minemust be well-held and well-guarded.What use are many disciplinesexcept for the discipline of guarding the mind?If one lives amidst wild, untamed people,one must carefully guard the wound,just as one guards a wound with care.Likewise, one must always guard this wound of the mind.If one is afraid of a minor wound's sufferingand guards the wound with care,why would one not guard the mind's woundfrom the fears of crushing and dismemberment?If one lives with such conduct,whether living among bad peopleor among women,the steadfast discipline will not be harmed.My gains, respect,body, and livelihood may be lost,and other good deeds may be lost,but the mind must never be lost.To those who wish to guard their minds,I implore you with joined palms:"Guard mindfulness and awarenesswith all your effort!"Just as people afflicted by illnessare powerless in all tasks,likewise, those whose minds are disturbed by delusionare powerless in all tasks.Even hearing, contemplating, and cultivatingwith a mind that lacks awareness,like water in a leaky pot,it does not remain in memory.Many learned, faithful,and diligent individuals,marred by the fault of lacking awareness,fall into downfalls.Robbers of unawareness,following the loss of mindfulness,even if merit is accumulated,they go to lower realms as if stripped by thieves.This multitude of troubling emotions, like robbers,seeks an opening.Once an opening is found, they steal good deedsand destroy the life of happy realms.Therefore, never let mindfulnessdepart from the gate of the mind.Even if it departs, recall the harms of lower realmsand bring it back close.From associating with a teacher,from the instructions of a master,and from fear, mindfulness easily arisesin those who are fortunate and respectful.The Buddhas and bodhisattvaspossess unobstructed vision everywhere."I always dwell in the presenceof all of them,"Thinking thus, one feels shame,respect, and fear, and likewise caution.Therefore, the recollection of the Buddhasalso arises repeatedly in that person.When mindfulness remains at the gate of the mindfor the sake of guarding,then awareness will arise,and what was lost will also return.First, knowing that this mindis flawed in this way,at that time, I must remainas inert as a piece of wood.I must never lookaimlessly at distractions.With focused attention, I must alwayslower my gaze and look.For the sake of resting my gaze,I may occasionally look in a direction.If someone appears in my sight,I should look and offer a welcome.To check for dangers on the road and so forth,I should repeatedly look in the four directions.After resting, I should turn my head andlook behind me.Having checked ahead and behind,I should go or come.In all situations,I should act with appropriate knowledge."I will remain in this way with my body,"Having made this resolve,
